justification: A pairs a serif body with bold sans headings, which gives a clearer hierarchy than B's light section heads. B's sans body has letterspaced, hyphenated justification that reads tighter. A's body size is inconsistent: Participants is larger than Procedure. A's indented blocks with drop caps read well, though the cover page is mostly empty. B's banded header is efficient, but it separates the formula from its intro across the page break. Its section heads are thin, and both designs leave a sparse final page.

A uses a strong navy title band, running headers, and rule-separated sections that give a clear, modern hierarchy with comfortable sans-serif body text. B is a plain Times-style layout with numbered headings. It is serviceable, but it has tighter, denser text, a dangling formula at the page break, and an indented paragraph after the table. Both leave page 3 mostly empty and carry the same raw $s_p$ artifact.

A uses a consistent serif family with a calm navy header band. Its table aligns to the text column, and the page breaks are more even (10/13/7). B mixes a geometric sans heading with a serif body. In B, headings hang left of the indented table and body text, which gives a misaligned left edge. Its page breaks are lopsided (11/15/4), and page B3 is mostly empty.

Design A keeps consistent justified body text, numbered headings and clean running heads. It holds the references together on A3, leaving only the footnotes on A4. Design B is inconsistent: the Participants text on B2 is set larger and ragged while other paragraphs are justified, and the drop caps are irregular. References is demoted to a subheading and split across B3 and B4. B's rules give some structure, but the mismatched sizing breaks the rhythm.

Both designs present the same repeated-header table. A keeps its headings and body text on one consistent left margin and frames each page with matching header and footer bands. B outdents its headings past the table edge with rules that extend beyond the content, giving a misaligned, ragged left edge. B's title band also floats with an uneven offset.

A's last page is a lone orphaned image whose caption belongs to a section that ended on A3, leaving A4 mostly blank and disconnected. B keeps the saltings image beside its section text on B4 and uses a pull quote and serif type for a more cohesive editorial feel (B3). A's cover illustration is stronger (A1), and B's pages carry some text-size inconsistency (B2, B4), but B's flow and pairing of image to text are better overall.

A strands its saltings image alone on the final page, leaving it almost empty (A4), and its pull quote is a small, weak italic line (A3). B gives each section a sensible block: the saltings image sits beside its text (B4), the pull quote is set large (B3), and quote boxes are overlaid on full-width images (B2, B3). B's flat dark cover is plainer than A's illustrated cover (A1 vs B1), but its interior pages are better balanced.

A keeps one consistent body size with clear numbered bold headings and steady spacing. B's paragraphs swap between larger and smaller body sizes (Abstract and Participants large, Introduction and Procedure small), which breaks the rhythm. B's light section headings are weak, and 'References' is styled smaller than the other sections. B also splits the reference list across pages. B's dark cover is striking, but A's interior reads more cleanly.

The two designs share the same structure, a title band and a table that repeats its header across three pages. A sets the table in a serif with a quiet top rule and a thin footer, which looks refined. A's serif figures are slightly harder to scan in dense columns. B uses a clean sans with tabular-looking numerals and fits more rows on each page (B1, B2), so the table reads more efficiently. B also adds navy running header and footer bands with page numbers (B2, B3), which help orientation. The cost is that B's last page is left emptier.

A keeps the title, heading and table on one consistent left edge. Its sans table text reads cleanly, and the dark header and footer bands give continuation pages a framed, consistent look. B's body and table are indented relative to the hanging headings, which misaligns the left edge (B1, B3). B's serif table is lighter and less crisp, and its continuation pages lack any band. B's bolder headings are a small plus, but overall A is more coherent.

A keeps the Shed four image beside its own text on A2, while B strands that image alone at the top of B3, cut off from its story. B's pull quote on B3 leaves its closing paragraph orphaned at the top of B4. B also has odd hanging indents, with body text indented past its headings, and tightly tracked justified text. A's consistent serif and accent rules and bands read more cohesively. Both end with large empty space on the last page.

B opens with a strong illustrated cover and consistent header and footer bands. However, its last page is a lone orphaned image stranded at the top of a nearly blank page, cut off from its 'What comes next' section on B3. B's pull quote also shrinks to a timid indented italic line (B3). A keeps the saltings image beside its section text (A4) and gives the pull quote real display weight (A3). Its serif body with strong sans headings reads more refined. A has weaker spots: the shed image floats alone at the top of A3, the A1 cover is plain, and caption fonts are mixed. Even so, its pages hold together better overall.

In A, the caption for the photo on page 3 ends up stranded at the top of A4, cut off from its image. B keeps that caption with its image on B3. B's pull quote on B2 is given proper display weight, while A2's quote is small. B's typography is a more refined serif and its rule dividers keep a consistent rhythm. A's cover illustration is stronger, but the boxed text on A3 reads cramped next to the image.

The two designs carry nearly identical tables. B's numbered headings align flush with the table, and its header and footer bands give running context on continuation pages. A indents body text and tables away from the headings, which is mildly awkward. A has some hierarchy strength in its rule-separated headings, but its continuation pages lack the orientation bands that B provides.

A keeps the saltings image beside its section text on A4. B leaves its final image stranded alone on B4, separated from its text on B3, so most of that page is empty. A also gives the pull quote a proper display treatment (A3), while B shrinks it to a small italic line. B has a stronger illustrated cover (B1) and clean header and footer bands. Its justified body text is readable but dense and shows hyphenation breaks. A's mixed lead and body sizes are slightly uneven but more elegant.

A has an illustrated cover, consistent header and footer bands, and evenly set body text with numbered headings (A1–A3). Its main flaw is A4, where the saltings image sits alone on an almost empty page. B fills its last page better (B4), but its cover is plain (B1). Its paragraphs switch sizes from one to the next (B2, B4). The shed image is stranded at the top of B3, cut off from its section. Its tracked text reads less smoothly. On balance A is the more polished design.

The two designs share the same layout, table pagination and banded headers. B's bold numbered section headings ('1 Pipeline by Region', '2 Notes') stand out more clearly than A's light-weight headings, which are softened further by rules above them. B's serif body text in the table reads a little more clearly than A's thin, light sans. A wraps less in the Region column, but B still has the stronger hierarchy overall.

A's body text size is inconsistent: the abstract and Participants paragraphs are set larger than the Introduction and Procedure paragraphs on A2. Its heavy rule above every section also chops the flow, and its references split awkwardly across A3 and A4. B keeps one consistent body size. Its numbered sans headings give a clear hierarchy, the running headers carry section names, and spacing is even across B2–B3. B's title page is plainer and its title wraps to an orphan word, but overall it reads more coherently.

B's last page is an orphaned figure stranded alone, separated from its 'What comes next' text on B3, which wastes a page and breaks the flow. B's pull quote is a small indented italic line that barely registers, and its text wraps awkwardly under the figure on B2. A keeps the saltings image beside its own section on A4, and A3 gives the pull quote real presence. A has its own flaws: a sparse cover, inconsistent body sizes and leftover space on A3 and A4. B's cover illustration and header and footer bands are strong. On balance A reads more coherently.

A keeps related content together. Its stats and chart sit on the same page (A2), and the image caption stays directly under the story panel. B orphans the caption 'The Pellow youth crew's training ground' at the top of B4, separated from its image on B3. B also pulls the chart away from the stats, which leaves a large gap on B2. B's cover duplicates the sunset image that appears again on B2, which feels redundant. B's bolder numbered headings are clear, but A flows more tightly across fewer pages.

B adds a dark cover, rules and running footers, but its body text changes size between paragraphs: the Abstract and Participants text is visibly larger than the Introduction and Procedure text (B2). Its light, unnumbered headings also read weaker than A's bold numbered ones. A is plain but consistent, compact and clearly ordered throughout (A1, A2).

A keeps the stat row with its "What changed" intro on A2 and sets the pull quote as a large serif statement, so the hierarchy reads clearly. B separates the stats from their intro, leaving a large gap at the bottom of B1 and an orphaned stat row on B2. B also shrinks the quote to small italics squeezed under the caption. B's side-by-side callout and image on B2 is cleaner than A's overlay, but A's serif typography and dedicated cover feel more polished overall.

Both share the same layout and table structure. A's bold numbered section headings ("1 Pipeline by Region", "2 Notes") stand out more clearly than B's light, thin headings. A's serif body text with a bold sans heading reads with stronger contrast. B's light grotesque in the table looks faint at small size, though its wider Region column wraps less.

B is preferred. Its numbered sans headings paired with serif body text give a clearer, more scholarly hierarchy. The formula stays with its sentence on B2, and the results, discussion and references sit together on B3. A splits the formula from 'computed as' across A1 and A2, and its many divider rules fragment the flow. A's light headings are weaker than its bold subheads, which inverts the hierarchy. B pays for a sparse title page and an orphaned footnote page (B1, B4), but A also leaves a mostly empty last page (A3).

A pairs a serif body with sans headings and uses a slightly narrower measure, which reads more comfortably than B's light, wide sans lines. In B, the paragraph on B2 wraps awkwardly under the figure, leaving a single orphaned line below the image. A's section numbering adds clear structure. Both designs end with a lone image on the last page (A4, B4). A's caption on A4 breaks awkwardly, a minor flaw.

The two tables are nearly identical. A's bold sans headings ("Pipeline by Region", "Notes") stand out more clearly from the serif body text than B's light serif headings, which blend into the text. B has a slightly wider Region column with less wrapping and a thin rule at the top of continuation pages, but A's stronger heading hierarchy gives it a small edge.

Design A has a dark cover page and a refined serif with rules, but the body text size is inconsistent. The Abstract and Participants paragraphs on A2 are set noticeably larger than the Introduction and Procedure text. Its heavy top bars and section rules also add visual clutter. Design B uses a consistent body size and numbered headings for a clear hierarchy. Its layout is compact, with no wasted cover page. Both share the unrendered '$s_p$' and a mostly empty final page.

Both designs share the same table structure. A's sans-serif type keeps the tabular figures crisper and easier to scan in dense numeric columns. A's running header and footer bands give each page a clear frame and context. A also fills page 2 more fully, leaving a lighter final page. B's serif text is small and thin, which makes the numbers harder to read, and its minimal footers give the pages less structure.

B uses a refined serif with a dedicated cover. The pull quote is given real prominence, and on B2 the stats sit right under "What changed". On B3 the story text is overlaid on the image as a contained callout. A's pull quote on A1 is weak small italic. The white-on-teal story box on A2 sits awkwardly beside the image with a narrow, ragged text column. A1 also ends with a dangling section start. Both end with a mostly empty final page.

A mixes inconsistent body sizes. The Abstract and Participants text is larger and loosely leaded, while Introduction and Procedure are smaller. Body text is also indented away from headings, and the drop caps feel ornamental. B keeps one consistent body size and numbered headings, with tidy running headers. A's display type is a bit more refined, but B reads more evenly. Both end with a near-empty last page.

Both designs share the same flaws: inconsistent body text sizes between sections and a leftover raw $s_p$ in the text. A's single serif family and dark cover read as calm and coherent. B mixes a heavy geometric sans for headings with a serif body and adds decorative drop caps to only some sections. Its indents shift from section to section, and its running footers show the wrong section names ("Participants" on page 2, "Analysis" on page 3). A's last page is also less sparse.

B is the more cohesive design. It has a dedicated cover, a consistent serif face, gold accent rules and a recurring header band, so the pages feel unified. A mixes a sans display face with serif body text and lets the full-bleed image break the margins. A also has outdented headings that misalign with the body, and its last page holds a single short paragraph with the rest left empty. B has some weaknesses: its chart is separated from its stats onto the next page, and page 4 is half empty. Even so, it reads as the more polished report.

A has an illustrated cover and consistent header/footer bands, and its image-plus-pullquote panels sit side by side cleanly. Its shed image wraps beside the text on A2. Its weakness is A4, an orphaned saltings image on an otherwise empty page. B's cover is a plain dark page. In B the shed image is stranded at the top of B3, far from its text. B's overlay boxes cover much of the illustrations, and its lede paragraphs are oversized. B's page 4 is about half empty, and its indentation changes from paragraph to paragraph. On balance A reads more coherently.

A runs as one consistent sans-serif article. Its banded title opens straight into content, and the type size and measure stay uniform throughout. B spends a mostly empty title page (B1). Inside, the text size jumps between sections: Participants is larger than Procedure on B2. Some paragraphs are justified and others ragged, and the drop caps clash with the sections that lack them (B2, B3). The result is uneven rhythm and wasted pages. Both designs leave a largely blank final page (A3, B4).

A keeps the saltings image beside its text on A4 and gives the pull quote real display weight on A3, so the hierarchy reads clearly. B has the richer illustrated cover on B1 and well-built header/footer bands. However, B strands the saltings image alone on a near-empty final page (B4), detached from its section. B's pull quote on B3 shrinks to a faint italic line. A has some awkward gaps of its own: the orphaned image at the top of A3 and lots of white space on A4. Even so, its image-text pairing and tone feel more deliberate.

A pairs a sans heading face with a serif body, has running headers, and keeps section blocks intact, which gives it a clearer hierarchy and a more polished look. Its drawbacks are a mostly empty title page and a final page holding only footnotes. B is compact but plain Times throughout. It splits the equation's explanation across pages B1–B2 and breaks the reference list across B2–B3, leaving a largely empty last page too. Both show the same raw $s_p$ artefact.

A has a proper cover and consistent header/footer bands, and its numbered headings sit flush with the body text. Its chart and photo panel use the brand teal. Its weak point is on A4, where the photo caption is orphaned at the top of the page, separated from its image on A3. B's headings hang outside the text column, and the stats and chart turn black, off-palette. B4 is almost entirely empty. B3's dark text box covering the image is heavier, and its full-bleed photo on B1 crowds the title band.

A has a dedicated full cover, a consistent serif system with orange accent rules, and a contained image within margins. B bleeds the hero image edge to edge, hanging it awkwardly under the header band, and its outdented headings with indented body text look misaligned. B's chart is plain black, and B4 holds only two lines on an otherwise empty page. A4 also ends sparse, but A keeps a steadier palette and rhythm throughout.

B has a strong cover and coherent teal bands, but its flow breaks badly. The chart is split from its stats onto B3. The Pellow image caption is orphaned at the top of B4, away from its image. The pull quote is shrunk to a small italic line. A keeps each figure with its caption and the chart with its stats. It gives the quote real presence and has a clean table. Its main flaw is a near-empty last page (A4).

A has bolder sans headings with hanging-indent bodies, which gives it a clear hierarchy. However, the Shed four image is orphaned at the top of A3, detached from its section. A3 also leaves a stray fragment sitting above the A4 heading, and A4's body column is narrow and widely tracked. B pairs the shed image with its text on B2 and keeps full-width body text consistently. B's accent bands and running header give it steady rhythm, though its light serif headings are somewhat weak.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so the section breaks stand out more clearly than B's light serif headings, which sit close to the body weight. A has quirks of its own: its drop caps are uneven, the Participants body is set larger than nearby paragraphs, and its running footers show odd labels. B has the same mixed body sizes and a heavy dark cover, but its accent rule nearly disappears against that cover. Overall A's hierarchy reads more crisply.

A pairs a bold heading face with a serif body. That gives clearer section headings: "Pipeline by Region" and "Notes" are bold, while B sets them in light weight. A's page furniture is also quieter. B's heavy dark header and footer bars on every continuation page compete with the table. The tables are essentially equivalent in both designs. B's sans text is slightly smaller and lighter, which makes it marginally harder to read.

Design B frames the paper with a dark title band, running headers and footers with page numbers, and rule-separated sections, which makes it easier to navigate and gives it a more finished feel. Its light-weight section heads, which drop the numbering, are weaker than A's bold serif numbered heads. Design A is a plain, conventional academic layout with tidy serif text, but it has less structure. Both have the same mostly empty final page and the same table. B's formula is split from its introducing sentence across pages B1 and B2; A keeps them together on A1.

Both designs present the same repeated-header table split across three pages. B's bold sans headings ('1 Pipeline by Region', '2 Notes') stand out more clearly than A's light serif headings. Its header and footer bands, with running section and page labels, also give stronger orientation. B fits more rows per page, so its last page is fuller. A has a heavier rule above each heading and lighter navigation, which makes it feel slightly less structured.

Design A keeps each section with its content. The "What changed" heading sits directly above its stats and chart (A2), the pull quote gets prominent display treatment, and the bold Montserrat headings give clear hierarchy. Its weaknesses are a near-empty final page (A4) and a full-bleed image that breaks the margins on A1. Design B strands the "What changed" heading at the foot of B1, away from its stats on B2. The volunteers paragraph is orphaned at the top of B3, and the quote shrinks to small grey italic. B's light, uniform headings weaken hierarchy, though its header and footer bands and tighter page count help a little.

B pairs a sans-serif heading face with a warm serif body, and its rule bands, drop caps and running footers give clearer section structure. Its table has a cleaner header rule. However, its body text size is inconsistent, larger in Participants on B2 than in Procedure, and it spends a whole page on a sparse cover. A is plain but consistent: compact Times-style text, though its justified spacing is tight. Both leave raw '$s_p$' text and end on a mostly empty final page. Overall, B reads as more polished.

Both designs share the same structure, and both strand the saltings image alone on a mostly empty last page. A keeps each section together. Its page 2 wraps the final paragraph under the figure, and page 3 holds two complete sections. B splits the smokehouse paragraph across pages 2 and 3, leaving a gap under the image on B2 and an orphaned fragment at the top of B3. B's serif body is pleasant and its numbered heads help navigation, but they are a minor gain. B's last caption also wraps awkwardly ('planted in / 2024.').

A keeps the photo caption attached to its image on A3. B orphans the Pellow caption at the top of B4, away from its picture on B3. A's pull quote is large and set off with rules on A2, which gives the page a clear emphasis. B's quote on B2 is small and tucked under the caption. B's cover image and header and footer bands are attractive, but the detached caption and weaker quote treatment hurt it. A's elegant serif and rule system read more cohesively.

A uses a compact title band and starts the content on page 1. Its body type is consistent and its running headers are clear. B spends a full dark cover page on a short paper, so the document stretches to four pages with a nearly empty last page. B's body text size is also inconsistent: the abstract and Participants sections are set larger than the Introduction and Procedure (B2). Both designs show the raw $s_p$ formula glitch and the same orphaned reference spill.

A uses a serif body with numbered bold headings that read clearly, and sections fill the pages cleanly. Its cost is a near-empty cover and a nearly empty footnote page (A1, A4). B's navy title band is strong, but its light-weight section headings are weaker than the bold subheadings. B also splits the equation from its lead-in sentence across pages and the reference list across pages (B1, B2, B3). Its footnotes sit right under the references with no separation.

A's bold sans section headings with numbers stand out more clearly than B's light serif headings, and its running header and footer bands give the pages a firm frame. B's table wraps 'Ahead of / plan' awkwardly in the Status column. B's 'Middle East &' line breaks are also clumsy. A's table columns feel tidier. Both designs paginate similarly.

A pairs a refined serif-and-sans palette with drop caps, but its text sizes are inconsistent. The Participants paragraph on A2 is set noticeably larger than the paragraphs around it. The Abstract is indented, yet the Introduction body wraps out to the margin under the drop cap. A3 uses heavy rules between every section. The running footers are wrong: "Participants" on A2 and "Analysis" on A3. A also spends a full cover page on a short paper. B is plain Times-style academic formatting. Its numbering is consistent and its body measure and size stay even throughout. The table on B2 is clean, and the text flows evenly across B1–B2. Both designs leave a raw $s_p$ in the text and end on a mostly empty last page.

Design A holds a consistent column. It keeps the color accent through the stats, chart and bands, and fits the content into three pages. Design B spreads it over four pages. B leaves a large empty gap under the full-bleed image on B1 and runs onto a near-empty page for one short section on B4. Its headings hang outside an indented text column, and its black chart loses the brand color. A's story block sits beside its image rather than covering it. A does leave some blank space at the bottom of A3.

B pairs a sans heading face with a serif body, adds running headers and footers, and gives references and the table more breathing room, which makes it easier to read. Its weaknesses are a sparse title page, an "Abstract" numbered as a section, and an orphaned footnote page (B4). A splits the formula explanation across pages and leaves page 3 mostly blank (A2, A3). A is compact and clean, but its Times layout is plainer and denser.

A opens with a full illustrated cover, which is attractive, but its body pages have problems. The caption "The Pellow youth crew's training ground" is stranded at the top of A4, cut off from its image on A3. A3 also opens with a chart that has no heading above it. B keeps that caption directly under its image on B2 and groups the stat row with the chart. B's tighter three pages keep sections moving, with orange rules marking each break. The cost is a large empty bottom on B1, though A2 and A4 have similar voids. Overall, B pairs content more coherently.

A's Garamond-style serif is elegant, but its body text size varies inconsistently between sections: the Abstract and Participants text on A2 is noticeably larger than the Introduction and Procedure text. A also spends a full dark cover page on just a title, which inflates the document to four pages for very little content. B keeps the body size consistent and opens with a compact title band, so content starts on B1. Its running header bands with section labels aid navigation, and the document fits in three pages. B's split equation across pages is a minor flaw. Both end on a mostly empty references page, as on A4 and B3.
